subject: Communication
title: Constructive Journalism: Reporting Solutions
description: A quick win: understand Constructive Journalism: Reporting Solutions.

hook.text: Danish news outlet Dagbladet shifted from pure problem-reporting to also covering solutions. Readership soared.

buildup.text: Constructive journalism doesn't ignore problems. It covers them AND asks: 'What's being done? What works?'

discovery.text: Solution-focused stories increase reader engagement, sense of agency, and willingness to act — without sugar-coating reality.

twist.text: Critics call it 'happy news' or naive. Proponents argue traditional journalism's exclusive focus on problems creates helplessness.

climax.text: The Solutions Journalism Network now trains reporters worldwide. Evidence-based solutions coverage is growing across newsrooms.

punchline.text: Good journalism shows what's broken. Great journalism also shows what's being.

quiz.question: What does constructive journalism add to traditional reporting?

details.summary: Constructive journalism covers problems and their potential solutions, providing a more complete and actionable picture of the world. Rather than just reporting what went wrong, it asks what is working and what can be learned. Research shows it increases engagement without sacrificing accuracy.
details.whyItMatters: Constructive journalism counters sensationalism's negativity bias by showing what is working, fostering informed engagement rather than helpless despair.
takeaways: Constructive journalism covers both problems and solutions
It increases engagement without sacrificing accuracy
It counters negativity bias in traditional news coverage

faq.question: Is constructive journalism the same as positive news?
faq.answer: No. Positive news ignores problems and focuses only on feel-good stories. Constructive journalism covers real problems rigorously but adds reporting on evidence-based solutions and lessons from places that have addressed similar challenges. It is about completeness, not cheerfulness.

faq.question: Does reporting on solutions make people complacent?
faq.answer: Research shows the opposite. Solutions-focused reporting actually increases people's sense of agency and willingness to take action. Problem-only reporting leads to helplessness and disengagement. When people see that solutions are possible, they become more motivated to contribute to change.
